title: BUG: Fix issue with GUI plotting malfunctioning when using an interactive interpreter
body:
When launching the GUI from a Jupyter notebook or similar interactive tool, an 'inline' backend for matplotlib is used by the default. This captures or breaks the graph windows created by the GUI and doesn't seem to work with the pipe that is used for plotting.

The existing workaround added in bd2bea0aec4871b2313fbebbf62e81b09129e2b6 no longer works because Jupyter seems to now default to a backend with a different name ('module://matplotlib_inline.backend_inline'). Here, a different test is used to detect an 'inline' backend.

Closes: ase/ase#1854

comments.author: askhl
lempelto
comments.body:
At first the envvar seems like a weird way to handle this but I don't know if there are any which are clearly better. `matplotlib.get_backend()` is a slightly more elegant way to retrieve the backend and should always give a value, unlike `MPLBACKEND` which may not exist. But I guess there aren't any downsides to using the envvar either. However, manipulating the variable may the most convenient way to take action once we know which backend is in use. There are three ways to set a backend: `MPLBACKEND`, `rcParams['backend']`, and `matplotlib.use()`. The problem is that one can only use the last two after matplotlib has been imported and a new import statement seems to erase the choice. Thus, all the points in the GUI code where matplotlib is imported and used would need to be modified (which isn't impossible, of course). On the other hand, setting the envvar is global (and also takes priority over rcParams)

A test would be nice, but it probably is tricky since this is a problem that mainly affects specific frameworks. But I'll modify the comments in the code at some point to give an explanation as to what's going on.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests using get_backend() instead of checking an envvar, and explicitly requests explanatory comments or tests to protect the logic from accidental reversion.

comments.body:
Since we are `main()` in this case, we are actually allowed to set envvars, globals and do other unlibrarylike things.

Cleanup should technically be inside try/finally, otherwise our change would leak to the caller in case of a crash (but we are main() there is no caller)

Since this is unimportant I'll merge anyway.
